comparator.name: Educational Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The full-time degree has a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling electives. The major includes required courses, major electives and a 15 EC thesis. This example follows the recommended first-year electives and leaves the remaining choices open.
components: Introduction to Research Methods and Statistics
Philosophy of Science and History of Education
Developing Assessment and Evaluation Tools for Education
Learning in Organizations: Interventions for Change
Choose a course from the approved major list.
Choose three courses from the approved major list.
Choose six courses. At least 15 EC must be at intermediate level or higher.

core: Learning, motivation and development across individual, social and organisational contexts
Education in society: inequality, policy, institutions and public purposes
Educational research, statistics, assessment and evidence-informed improvement
Learning-environment and instructional design, with an acknowledged UCR specialist-coverage limit
adjacent: Educational technology, digital learning and digital resources
Organisational learning, leadership, policy and workplace development
Educational philosophy, inclusion, language and professional advising
questions: How do people learn and develop across individual, social and organisational settings?
How can empirical evidence improve learning, assessment, organisations and educational policy?
How can effective learning environments and technology-supported education be designed and evaluated responsibly?

alternatives.label: Learning, Development and Social Research
alternatives.concept: Study how people learn and develop, and how social institutions shape their opportunities. Use psychology, sociology and research methods to examine learning, inequality and public policy.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how people learn and develop, and how social institutions shape their opportunities. Use psychology, sociology and research methods to examine learning, inequality and public policy.
progression: Social and behavioral foundations precede advanced research methods, policy analysis and lifespan development.

alternatives.label: Cognition, Communication and Learning Technology
alternatives.concept: Study how attention, memory, language and development shape learning. Use statistics and computing to investigate behavior and understand digital tools, and apply communication skills in public settings.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how attention, memory, language and development shape learning. Use statistics and computing to investigate behavior and understand digital tools, and apply communication skills in public settings.
alternatives.distinctness: Study how attention, memory, language and development shape learning. Use statistics and computing to investigate behavior and understand digital tools, and apply communication skills in public settings. Each plan has 17 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.
progression: Brain and behavior precedes advanced cognition. Programming and mathematics precede machine learning, and introductory rhetoric precedes community practice.

alternatives.label: Organizational Learning, Policy and Leadership
alternatives.concept: Study how organizations lead change and how public institutions make policy. Use organizational psychology, leadership, negotiation and research methods to examine workplace development and decisions about learning.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how organizations lead change and how public institutions make policy. Use organizational psychology, leadership, negotiation and research methods to examine workplace development and decisions about learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Study how organizations lead change and how public institutions make policy. Use organizational psychology, leadership, negotiation and research methods to examine workplace development and decisions about learning. Each plan has 14 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 19 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.
progression: Business, research methods and leadership communication precede organizational psychology, negotiation and policy analysis.

selection.assessment: Three related plans emphasize learning and social research, cognition and computing, or organizational and policy study. The plans build supporting disciplines for educational questions. Dedicated curriculum design, educational technology design, assessment instruments and the supervised educational research thesis remain material gaps.

blocks: Utrecht introduces education as a field of study. UCR approaches learning through psychology, society and research.
Utrecht teaches introductory design of learning environments.
Both examine psychological development. Utrecht focuses on learning and instruction.
Utrecht teaches advanced instructional design using the Four-Component Instructional Design model.
Utrecht studies the history of education and the philosophy of educational research.
Utrecht studies the use of technology in education. UCR develops general computing and digital skills.
Utrecht develops instruments for educational assessment and evaluation.
Both examine organizational behavior. Utrecht focuses on learning at work.
Utrecht examines interventions for organizational learning and change.
Research, ethics, academic development and choice space
Both develop research design and introductory statistics.
Both apply quantitative methods to empirical research.
Both develop methods for evaluating research evidence. Utrecht applies its methods to education.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC thesis after the three research methods courses. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose one additional major elective after the two recommended courses shown.
Choose three major electives. Options include educational action research, multilingual education and international education.
Choose 45 EC of profiling electives, including at least 15 EC at intermediate level or higher.

notes.text: The UCR plans explore learning through psychology, computing, communication or organizational study. Utrecht provides dedicated instructional design, educational assessment and a required educational research thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: This mainly Dutch-taught bachelor studies how people learn, how learning environments are designed and how research informs education.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Utrecht combines a 135 EC major with 45 EC of profiling electives. The UCR options emphasize learning and social research, cognition and technology, or organizational learning and policy.
